assessments.reasoning: The retained July 2024 Oracle original distinguishes the language from the accompanying tools. Its cover establishes a different edition. The October 2022 SQR original supplies the evidence for the dated claim.

The retained Oracle cover identifies a July 2024 manual for PeopleCode within PeopleTools 8.60. It establishes a subject boundary. The SQR definition and its October 2022 attribution both come from the earlier SQR manual.

Opening the retained original established the edition from its cover. Page 15 assigns enterprise-data access, manipulation and reporting to SQR as a programming language. Its tool list separately describes execution of compiled programs and printer configuration. Together the two pages support the full identity claim within SQR for PeopleSoft. The two July 2024 references serve only to distinguish editions and subjects.

challenge.method: Compare the edition dates even where the descriptive passages match. Test whether the common PeopleTools version identifies the same language reference. Check whether the three data operations describe only the overall reporting system.
challenge.results: The compared page 15 excerpts have identical bytes across editions. Their covers differ, so the later passage supplies edition context only. The cover names a different language and date. It contributes no SQR definition or independent corroboration. The language-specific subsection assigns all three operations to the language itself. The surrounding list distinguishes SQR Execute and SQR Print.

limitations: The registry name denotes the documented language in the PeopleSoft product. It covers neither SQR Execute and SQR Print nor extensions in other vendor or PeopleTools editions.
